text: As Jesus went along, he saw a man blind from birth.
His disciples asked, 'Rabbi, who sinned — this man or his parents — that he was born blind?'
Jesus answered, 'Neither this man nor his parents sinned; he was born blind so that God's work could be shown in him.'
'We must carry out the work of the one who sent me while it is still day; night is coming, when no one can work.'
'As long as I am in the world, I am the world's light.'
Saying this, Jesus spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and spread it on the man's eyes.
'Go,' he told him, 'wash in the Pool of Siloam' (the name means Sent). So the man went, washed, and came back able to see.
His neighbors and those who had known him as a beggar asked, 'Isn't this the man who used to sit and beg?'
Some said, 'It's him'; others said, 'No, he just looks like him.' The man himself kept saying, 'I am the one.'
'Then how were your eyes opened?' they asked.
He answered, 'A man named Jesus made mud, put it on my eyes, and told me to go wash in Siloam. So I went, washed, and could see.'
'Where is he?' they asked. 'I don't know,' he said.
They brought the man who had been blind to the Pharisees.
Now the day Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes was a Sabbath.
So the Pharisees also questioned him about how he had received his sight. 'He put mud on my eyes,' the man told them, 'I washed, and now I see.'
Some of the Pharisees said, 'This man is not from God, since he does not keep the Sabbath.' Others asked, 'How can a sinner perform such signs?' And they were divided.
So they asked the blind man again, 'What do you say about him, since it was your eyes he opened?' 'He is a prophet,' the man replied.
The Jews still did not believe he had been blind and had received his sight until they sent for his parents.
'Is this your son?' they asked. 'Do you claim he was born blind? How can he now see?'
His parents answered, 'We know this is our son, and that he was born blind.'
'But how he can now see, or who opened his eyes, we don't know. Ask him — he's old enough to speak for himself.'
His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders, who had already agreed that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be thrown out of the synagogue.
That was why they said, 'He's old enough; ask him.'
A second time the Pharisees summoned the man and said, 'Give glory to God. We know this man is a sinner.'
He answered, 'Whether he is a sinner, I don't know. One thing I know — I was blind, and now I see.'
'What did he do to you?' they asked. 'How did he open your eyes?'
He replied, 'I already told you, and you didn't listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you want to become his disciples too?'
Then they hurled insults at him: 'You are his disciple; we are disciples of Moses.'
'We know God spoke to Moses, but as for this fellow, we don't even know where he comes from.'
The man answered, 'That's remarkable — you don't know where he's from, yet he opened my eyes.'
'We know God doesn't listen to sinners, but he listens to the godly person who does his will.'
'Never before has anyone heard of someone opening the eyes of a person born blind.'
'If this man weren't from God, he could do nothing.'
They answered, 'You were born entirely in sin, and you dare to lecture us!' And they threw him out.
Jesus heard they had thrown him out, and finding him, he asked, 'Do you believe in the Son of Man?'
'Who is he, sir?' the man asked. 'Tell me, so I may believe in him.'
'You have already seen him,' Jesus said. 'In fact, he is speaking with you now.'
'Lord, I believe,' the man said, and worshiped him.
Jesus said, 'I came into this world for judgment, so that the blind may see and those who see may become blind.'
Some Pharisees standing nearby heard this and said, 'Are we blind too?'
Jesus said, 'If you were blind, you would not be guilty of sin; but since you claim you see, your guilt remains.'
